analysis_plan.rationale: Two independent windows of continuous resolution hours -- Welch's t is the engine's two-independent-means default.

changes.text: Assign-on-arrival dispatch rule: kill the once-a-day triage batch; each new routine ticket is assigned within the hour by a rotating dispatcher-of-the-day.

comparison_design.description: The frozen July baseline (tickets-baseline.csv, n=127, mean 26.71, stable) vs the measured after window.

demand.note: No other volume change beyond the onboarding class noted above.

measurement.note: Same operational definition and extraction procedure as the baseline; T-12 still stands.

other.note: No ticketing-system or approval-policy change landed in the window.

season.note: Fall onboarding class of 14 new hires starts 2026-09-21, inside the after window -- can only push access-grant volume (and resolution times) up, never manufacture a win.

staffing.note: Same three techs and dispatch lead throughout.

artifact.falsification_line: Two settled weeks above 12.0 business hours -> revert to batch triage and take the next-ranked cause.

inclusion.honesty_note: Same desk, same techs as the baseline -- no randomization across sites.
inclusion.how_selected: Same systematic every-2nd-ticket rule as the baseline
inclusion.who_or_what: All routine (P3) tickets, all three techs, both channels, every 2nd ticket sampled -- the T-11 collection plan's rule

artifact.notes: One change only -- a draft bundling the access matrix into the same pilot was refused with EXIT-10, and the access matrix stayed queued for its own later pilot.
